problem: The existing CI-triggered Codex request controller prevents repeated requests for one commit but has no cap across PR commits. Repeated implementation/review exchanges could continue indefinitely or keep chasing low-severity findings.
solution: Add a deterministic per-PR review budget derived from owner-authored SHA-tagged request comments, bot-authored Codex review statuses and inline findings. Round zero is the initial review; allow five total repair reviews, P1 five, P2 three, P3 one, with two unchanged substantive repair outcomes triggering a review hold. Do not request Codex when prior receipt is pending. On terminal stop PATCH the PR body with **REVIEW HOLD:**; the existing readiness gate rejects held PRs. Extend agent policy and CI tests. No auto-merges.
tests: Node review budget unit tests for initial round, P1/P2/P3 limits, no-progress, missing evidence, duplicate SHA and untrusted input
Codex request controller integration tests for P3 hold and no requests while prior review is pending
Full repository CI: lint, format, typecheck, unit tests, build, package check, Storybook
risks: Codex inline severity is inferred only from its bot-authored [P1]/[P2]/[P3] annotations; missing/ambiguous priority gets P1-level budget. Identification of repeated findings uses a normalized file path and first-line title, so owner may review a false-positive repeat. Receipt and pagination failures deny retries; holds require owner intervention. Existing old request markers are counted, so budgets survive deployment.
review: Check exact SHA matching, prior review completion/receipt checks, bot-only severity evidence, commit-independent counting, P1 five / P2 three / P3 one and global five repair ceilings, two unsuccessful repair-round cutoff, PR body review hold, no auto merge, and tests for unauthorized comments and incomplete reviews.
